title: Printability gate is a scalar max-dimension test and cannot detect a part that does not fit the bed
evidence: src/satellite1_ultra/validation.py:1533 sets `limit = 256.0` and line 1536 reduces each part to `largest = max(box.xlen, box.ylen, box.zlen)`.
Line 1546 then reports `status = PASS if largest <= limit`, so the only quantity compared is a single scalar against a single scalar.

The check therefore has no concept of a rectangular bed, no separate Z limit, and no orientation feasibility test. A 256 x 256 x 256 mm part passes on every machine, and a 192 x 212 mm part passes on a 100 x 100 mm bed.

outer_shell is 192.0 x 212.0 x 189.0 mm in its required upright orientation (reports/validation/printability.json, part `outer_shell`), and reports `status: PASS` with `largest_dimension_mm: 212.0` against `build_envelope_mm: 256.0`.

docs PRINTING_GUIDE.md (generated by src/satellite1_ultra/documentation.py:1153-1165) states the real requirement in prose: 'Absolute usable travel: 212 x 192 x 189 mm', 'Practical minimum: 220 x 220 x 200 mm only when the full 220 mm is usable', and 'In-plane rotation cannot fit the shell on a 210 x 210 mm bed.'
No automated gate enforces any of those three statements; they are unverified prose.
anti_slip_ring at 188 x 208 mm and electronics_shroud at 185 x 205 mm sit within a few mm of the same limit and are likewise unchecked.

Project owner reports the target machine is a modified Ender 5 with X measured at 220 mm and Y unmeasured but believed smaller, possibly ~200 mm. At Y = 200 the shell fits only when oriented 212 along X, leaving 4 mm per edge. At the 190 mm Y first reported by the owner it does not fit in any orientation.
engineering_consequence: The gate that exists specifically to prevent an unprintable release cannot detect the failure mode it was written for. A builder whose bed is smaller than the undocumented-in-code 220 x 220 requirement receives a package whose automated report says PASS, and discovers the problem only after a multi-day ASA print fails or is refused by the slicer. Because the constraint lives only in generated prose, any future change to enclosure width or grille margin can silently push the shell past a real bed without any check failing.
verification_method: Reproduce: run `.venv/bin/python -c "import json; d=json.load(open('reports/validation/printability.json')); print([p for p in d['parts'] if p['part']=='outer_shell'])"` and observe PASS at 212.0 mm against a 256.0 mm scalar. Then confirm the gate is orientation- and bed-blind by temporarily setting `limit = 150.0` in validation.py:1533 and re-running; parts fail on the scalar only, and no part is ever reported as unfittable on a rectangular bed. Fix by replacing the scalar with a per-axis build volume (x, y, z) sourced from config, testing both in-plane orientations of each part footprint, and failing when neither orientation fits.

title: Configured printing.maximum_build_dimension is dead configuration
evidence: grep across src/satellite1_ultra for `maximum_build_dimension` returns no consumer; DesignParameters has no corresponding field and configuration.py does not map the `printing` block.
src/satellite1_ultra/validation.py:1533 hardcodes the same value as `limit = 256.0` instead of reading it.

MUTATION TEST performed 2026-07-29: config/default.yaml printing.maximum_build_dimension mutated 256.0 -> 100.0, then printability_report(load_design_parameters()) was re-run. It still reported build_envelope_mm 256.0, outer_shell largest_dimension_mm 212.0, part status PASS and overall status PASS. The validation suite did not detect the mutation. Mutation restored and config/default.yaml verified clean against git.
engineering_consequence: Editing the documented build-volume knob in config/default.yaml changes nothing, so an operator retargeting the design to their own printer gets silent no-ops and a report that still claims a 256 mm envelope. This masks PRINT-001 by giving the appearance of a configurable gate.
verification_method: Set `printing.maximum_build_dimension: 100.0` in config/default.yaml, regenerate the printability report, and confirm `build_envelope_mm` is still 256.0 and every part still passes. Restore the file afterwards.
